The mind is doing everything that it can to avoid short-term pain,
and this can be seen in areas such as weight loss and making more money.
When we try to lose weight,
the mind isn't looking at the long-term pain that the added weight will have on our bodies,
it's looking at the short-term pain it will have when it goes through withdrawals of fat and sugar.
The body becomes accustomed to a certain type of intake of calories.
It becomes accustomed to consuming fat and sugar.
But, it's not just the physical addiction.
The body also uses food as an escape;
it's an emotion-numbing activity used as a defense mechanism to dealing with internal strife and conflict.
Again, this is where the mind thinks it's doing more to avoid pain than gain pleasure,
but it's focused on the short-term pain-and-pleasure paradigm.
Of course, it's easy to see where the potential for short-term pain holds us back when it comes to external substances, but how about when it comes to internal desires.
When we want to make more money, do you think all of us go out there, push and push until we start earning more?
No, of course not.
The mind wants us to have more money, but it doesn't necessarily want to have to go through tremendous amounts of pain in order to get that money.
But, that's just what's required of us when we're striving to accomplish something formidable such as acquiring large amounts of money or losing a tremendous amount of weight.
There are certain sacrifices that need to be made of not only our time, but also of our entire selves.
But, this is also why so many get-rich-quick schemes out there easily fool most people.
That's because the mind wants what it wants, but knows that it must function under the reality principle.
The reality principle states that the ego will attempt to give us what we want within reality.
The ego will grapple between the forces of the id and the superego by applying the reality principle.
But, when a get- rich-quick scheme seems so good that it might be true, the ego allows us to dive right in.
We fail to do the proper research on just what it's going to take make money with whatever program we sign up to.
When we're looking for a quick solution to our financial woes,
we generally approach things with blinders on.
And, this isn't just a problem that affects some people;
it's something that's widespread because it's a product of our own internal psychologies.
Our psychic apparatus pushes us towards the seemingly too-good-to-be-true offers.
Whether it's fad weight-loss diets, get-rich-quick schemes, or anything else,
if it seems to good to be true, it generally is.
But, that's not so according to our egos.
Once we order that system, we feel an instant calming effect.
But, that's a result of the easing of some internal pressures.
However, it doesn't stop there.
The issue at hand is that, most of us generally do want to take the easy way out.
We don't want to work and toil away endlessly towards the attainment of some hope or some dream.
We want what we want and we want it now.
And, when we're pushing towards a goal, we're too quick to give up because of a little bit of failure.
When we hit a roadblock, we tend to throw our hands up in silent resignation.
But, nothing in life is going to be easy that's worthwhile.
You're going to have to fail many times before you succeed.
The difference between a successful person and an unsuccessful one is that the former doesn't give up.
No matter how many times a successful-minded person fails, they always get back up.
They modify their approach and they keep trying again and again;
this is part of the art of persistence.
And, surviving failure isn't that difficult; it's more of the fear of failure that stuns us.
You can survive failure in your life; you've most likely already done so.
And, failure is a sign of life;
it's a sign that you're trying.
You have to keep persisting no matter what gets in your way.
If you were to ask Gandhi or Martin Luther King Jr. if they were still around today,
whether or not they were okay with the notion of failure,
they would have told you that it was preposterous.
They had a vision of freedom.
One had a vision for the freedom from British rule,
and the other for freedom from white oppression.
They certainly exercised the law of attraction,
because they kept that goal in their mind's eye and they didn't falter.
And, they pushed towards it by taking persistent action every single day.
Even when they failed and faced huge adversity, they kept on pushing.
Even when their people were jailed, shot, stabbed, and violated in every way, they kept on fighting.
You're going to fail in life no matter what you do.
And, the more times you fail, the more you're going to get closer to your goals.
If you ask some of the most successful people in the world what the secret to their success was,
it wouldn't be too much of a secret.
Persistence is the secret to success.
But, it's not just persistence in and of itself;
it's a combination of persistence with positive thoughts and focused actions.
You must be able to continue pushing towards your goal,
even after you fall down, and modify your approach along the way.
And, if you fail, it's okay.
Get back to the drawing board and see what you did wrong.
Try to look at things from a fresh perspective and see how you can modify your approach.
If you were to ask a mother who's watching their son or daughter try to walk for the first time,
whether or not they were afraid they wouldn't be able to walk because they kept falling down,
they would look at you with incredulity.
That mother would tell you that no matter how many times their son or daughter fell down, they would learn to walk.
And, the baby trying to walk isn't going to stop trying;
it's going to modify its approach to gain its balance until it succeeds.
Like a baby who's trying to walk for the first time or even talk, we must persist towards our goals.
As soon as the notion enters our mind that we might not be able to achieve something, everything will begin to go downhill from there.
Once we have a feeling that we cannot achieve something, we'll move towards failure because the mind will get what it focuses on.
If the mind, however, believes that no matter how many times we fail that we will succeed in our quest to accomplish something, we will.
There's something so powerful about the focused power of thought.
It can drive us to achieve anything.
In 1940, if you had asked any human being about the potential for commercial space travel, let alone sending a man to the moon, they would have thought you were certifiably insane.
But, as you can see, things are far different today because the focused power of thought has moved us towards the realization of something we once thought would have been impossible.
What was science fiction not too long ago is reality today.
Could you imagine telling that same individual from 1940 that we would be able to instantly communicate and share our photos, videos, and written communications via an interconnected always-on web?
They would have looked at you as if you had lost your mind.
All of what we have today is the product of our positive thoughts, but it's also the product of our failures.
It's through the failures that we were able to achieve the things that we have in our lives today.
None of our notable achievements throughout history came without major failure.
Rather, it was through that failure that the achievements were born.
When we have positive thoughts that we can achieve something, and we're able to push towards the realization of that, we can accomplish anything.
We're going to fail along the way many times over.
The more we fail, the closer we'll get to our goals.
Failure isn't something that should be feared, it should be something that's embraced, because without failure, we wouldn't be where we are today.
Don't be afraid to fail.
Don't be afraid of what others will think of you if you fail.
Look at the big picture, get up, and try again.
Keep trying and persisting until you reach all of your goals, no matter what.
vi: Thất bại có ý nghĩa gì?
Để tiếp tục tồn tại sau thất bại, để chiến thắng được nỗi sợ thất bại với cái gì đó trong cuộc sống,
ta cần hiểu rõ hơn về thất bại cùng ý nghĩa của nó.
Điều thường xảy ra với thất bại là ta để cho bản ngã kiểm soát mình.
Tôi không nói về bản ngã ở khía cạnh trừu tượng của từ ngữ.
Ở đây, tôi muốn nói về nó như một thành phần nằm bên trong bộ máy tâm thần.
Khi bản ngã giành được quyền kiểm soát, ta trở thành nô lệ của tâm trí.
Nhưng điều quan trọng cần nhớ là ý nghĩa của thất bại.
Thông thường, ta quá chú ý đến nỗi sợ thất bại đến nỗi ta chọn cách tồn tại an toàn nhất.
Thất bại thì sao?
Chẳng có gì sai với thất bại cả vì nó là cái định nghĩa ta.
Thất bại giúp ta có được sự hiểu biết sâu sắc hơn về những thứ sẽ không bao giờ xảy ra nếu cuộc sống cứ diễn ra giống như ta mong muốn.
Đôi lúc, khi ta đi chệch hướng, có một lý do sâu sắc hơn đằng sau điều ấy.
Khi nỗi đau chồng chất quá nhiều bên trong,
nó buộc bạn phải tìm kiếm tận sâu thẳm nội tâm để có được sự hiểu biết mới về cuộc sống của mình.
Nó buộc bạn thay đổi theo hướng tích cực.
Chính từ thất bại, cùng cảm giác đau khổ nó gây ra, mà ta mới đạt được nhiều tiến bộ, thành tựu to lớn trong khoa học, kỹ thuật, kinh doanh như ngày nay.
Thomas Edison cuối cùng cũng phát minh ra được bóng đèn điện thương mại hoạt động trong một thời gian dài sau khi thất bại cả 10000 lần.
Walt Disney đã tạo ra được một trong các thương hiệu nổi tiếng nhất trên hành tinh hiện nay sau khi bị phá sản và bị sa thải với những công việc trước đó vì lý do không có đủ khả năng sáng tạo.
Nhưng ngoài những người chuyển thất bại thành thành công nổi tiếng nhất, thì ngày nào cũng có người gặp thất bại rồi sau đó đạt được thành công to lớn.
Ngày nào cũng có người phải đấu tranh, vật lộn với nỗi đau khổ của thất bại nhưng họ vẫn biến thất bại ấy thành cái gì đó có giá trị.
Họ không để thất bại làm suy sụp tinh thần của mình.
Trái lại, họ còn tận dụng thất bại để truyền thêm động lực, tiếp thêm năng lượng cho mình để vươn lên trong tương lai.
Họ tìm kiếm tận trong sâu tâm hồn và thấy được lý do tại sao thất bại lại giúp họ trở nên tốt hơn.
Họ dùng thất bại để đẩy mình vượt ra khỏi các giới hạn hiện tại.
Trong cuộc sống, bạn cần tìm hiểu xem thất bại có ý nghĩa gì với mình.
Thất bại kìm hãm bước tiến của ta vì tâm lý tiềm thức của ta có khuynh hướng tránh đau khổ nhiều hơn là tìm kiếm niềm vui.
Vì vậy, nếu tâm trí sợ cái gì đó, nó không chỉ tập trung vào cái đó, mà còn hướng cuộc sống của ta về phía nó.
Đó là vì tâm trí sẽ di chuyển về phía cái mà nó tập trung vào.
Nếu tâm trí tập trung vào thất bại, ta sẽ đi về phía thất bại.
Nhưng nếu tâm trí tập trung vào thành công bằng mọi giá, nó sẽ đẩy ta đi về phía thành công.
Tuy nhiên, ta thường không chú ý đến việc tâm trí ảnh hưởng đến cuộc sống của bản thân, vì vậy ta để tiềm thức kiểm soát mình.
Bạn phải nhận biết các ý nghĩ nội tâm thật sự của mình, rồi thay đổi chúng theo hướng có lợi cho bạn.
Nếu trước đây, bạn từng sợ thất bại với việc gì đấy, bạn cần tìm hiểu xem nỗi sợ hãi ấy thật sự là gì, sau đó tìm cách loại bỏ nó.
Hãy nghĩ về điều này trong giây lát.
Hãy nghĩ lại cái mà bạn từng không dám làm vì sợ thất bại.
Nó là gì?
Có lẽ, bạn không dám thành lập công ty riêng, mua một ngôi nhà mới,
hay bắt đầu một mối quan hệ vì sợ những khả năng có thể xảy ra do nỗi sợ thất bại phỏng đoán.
Ý nghĩ nào xuất hiện trong đầu bạn.
Hãy lấy một tờ giấy và viết chúng ra để biết bạn sợ gì.
Thường thì những nỗi sợ hãi của ta khá cơ bản.
Chúng bắt nguồn từ bản năng tồn tại.
Nên nhớ, giống như bao sinh vật khác, con người cũng có bản năng sinh tồn ích kỷ mang tính di truyền.
Nhưng với ý thức của con người,
sự sinh tồn ở đây không chỉ là sinh tồn tự nhiên,
mà nó còn liên quan đến cả sự sinh tồn về mặt tài chính nữa.
Chính nỗi sợ cạn kiệt nguồn tài chính khiến nhiều người không dám bắt đầu sự nghiệp hay công việc mơ ước của họ.
Bây giờ, hãy viết ra mọi niềm hy vọng, ước mơ trước đây mà bạn không dám theo đuổi vì nỗi sợ hãi thầm lặng.
Điều quan trọng ở đây là bạn phải trung thực với bản thân vì bạn muốn biết các nỗi sợ hãi ấy thật ra là gì.
Khi đã phơi bày mọi nỗi sợ hãi ra ngoài ánh sáng rồi,
bạn có thể bắt đầu phân tích, mổ xẻ chúng.
Chia tờ giấy ra thành ba phần theo chiều dọc.
Cột đầu tiên bên trái, bạn viết ra mục tiêu hay niềm hy vọng mà mình đã từ bỏ trong quá khứ.
Dù nó là gì đi nữa, bạn cần phải viết nó rõ ràng, chi tiết.
Có lẽ, bạn bỏ cuộc với việc chuyển đến một thành phố mới để gầy dựng sự nghiệp.
Có lẽ, bạn bỏ cuộc với một cuộc hôn nhân hay mối quan hệ tiềm năng mới.
Dù các mục tiêu, hy vọng ấy là gì đi nữa, hãy viết chúng ra.
Hãy thành thật với bản thân.
Điều gì đấy sâu sắc sẽ xảy ra khi bạn tập trung vào bài tập thực hành này.
Đọc hay nghe tài liệu, thông tin thôi vẫn chưa đủ.
Nếu không hành động và thực hiện các bước đã được đề cập đến,
bạn không thể hy vọng mình sẽ nhận được kết quả tốt trong tương lai.
Hãy dành thời gian để làm bài thực hành này,
và làm nó bằng khả năng tốt nhất của bản thân.
Sau khi đã viết ra mục tiêu mà bạn bỏ cuộc, hãy viết ra lý do tại sao bạn lại bỏ cuộc vào cột ở giữa.
Nỗi sợ hãi tiềm ẩn mà bạn cố gắng tránh né là gì?
Hãy tìm kiếm câu trả lời thật kỹ trong tâm trí.
Việc này có thể rất khó vì bản ngã có cách che đậy hành vi của nó trong các câu trả lời hợp lý khéo léo.
Tuy nhiên, điều mà bản ngã làm chỉ là cố gắng bảo vệ bạn tránh được đau khổ,
nên nó sẽ làm mọi thứ có thể để che giấu sự thật.
Sau khi đã viết ra mọi nỗi sợ hãi hay lý do khiến mình từ bỏ mục tiêu,
tôi muốn bạn viết những lời mô tả xem cuộc sống của mình hiện tại sẽ ra sao nếu trước đây bạn không từ bỏ, vào cột thứ ba.
Tôi muốn bạn nghĩ xem mọi thứ sẽ khác biệt ra sao nếu bạn kiên trì với mục tiêu của mình và thành công.
Nếu bạn có thể vượt ra khỏi các giới hạn của hiện tại, chiến thắng nỗi sợ hãi, và hoàn thành được các mục tiêu của bản thân thì sao?
Nếu công ty bạn thành lập lớn mạnh và giúp bạn có được sự tự do về tài chính thì sao?
Nếu cuộc hôn nhân ấy thành công thì sao?
Nếu bạn mua được căn nhà mới hay đi học lại để tiếp thu thêm kỹ năng mới thì sao?
Điều gì sẽ xảy ra?
Hãy dành thời gian suy nghĩ để làm phần này, cũng như hai phần kia vậy.
Khi đã hoàn thành xong cả ba cột, hãy quan sát từng mục tiêu, rồi tiếp theo là từng nỗi sợ hãi đã gây trở ngại cho bạn.
Tiếp theo, quan sát những gì mà bạn sẽ đạt được nếu không từ bỏ mục tiêu trước đây.
Có lẽ, một vài người bạn của bạn đã tự mình thành lập công ty riêng của họ cũng vào thời điểm bạn muốn làm thế.
Bây giờ họ ra sao?
Nếu bạn cũng tự mở công ty riêng, thì giờ bạn sẽ ra sao?
Đây chỉ là những giả thuyết,
nhưng mục tiêu của bài thực hành này là giúp bạn thấy được nỗi sợ hãi gây trở ngại cho mình ra sao.
Nó khiến bạn bỏ lỡ cái gì trong cuộc sống?
Bạn bỏ cuộc như vậy có xứng đáng không?
Điều tồi tệ nhất có thể xảy ra nếu bạn thất bại là gì?
Hỏi bản thân những câu hỏi khó không phải là việc dễ dàng.
Tâm trí không muốn thừa nhận một số điều nhất định vì sợ điều ấy sẽ gây ra quá nhiều đau khổ cho cuộc sống của ta.
Thay vào đó, tâm trí muốn có được trạng thái cân bằng,
vì ở trạng thái ấy, ta sẽ hạnh phúc ở một mức độ nào đó.
Vì vậy, dù tâm trí cố gắng tránh đau khổ nhiều hơn là tìm kiếm hạnh phúc,
nhưng nó cũng có quan điểm thiên lệch về đau khổ trong mối quan hệ với không gian và thời gian.
Nó tìm cách né tránh đau khổ trước mắt thay vì lâu dài.
Điều này thể hiện rõ ở nhiều người, nhiều nền văn hóa, thành phố khác nhau trên thế giới.
Ví dụ, nhiều người không bỏ hút thuốc ngay cả khi họ biết hút thuốc có hại về lâu dài.
Dù biết hút thuốc lá gây ảnh hưởng xấu đến sức khỏe, thậm chí là gây ra bệnh nan y,
nhưng họ vẫn cứ hút thuốc.
Vì thế, nếu tâm trí thật sự cố gắng tránh né đau khổ về lâu dài,
bạn nghĩ nó sẽ cho phép một người hút thuốc ư?
Không, tâm trí chỉ cố gắng né tránh nỗi đau đớn, khổ sở trước mắt mà thôi,
vì việc bỏ hút thuốc trước mắt sẽ rất khổ sở.
Nó sẽ làm thay đổi cấu tạo hệ thần kinh của cơ thể.
Nó đòi hỏi bạn phải đoạn tuyệt với chất nicôtin.
Nhưng hút thuốc lá còn là một cách trốn tránh về mặt cảm xúc,
chứ không phải chỉ là một thói nghiện không thôi.
Tâm trí tạo ra mối liên kết giữa việc hút thuốc với sự làm giảm bớt mọi nỗi lo âu thông qua tác động của chất nicôtin.
Thế nên, dù biết hút thuốc lá sẽ gây ra nỗi đau đớn, khổ sở về lâu dài, nhưng ta vẫn cứ làm việc này.
Tâm trí sẽ làm mọi thứ có thể để tránh nỗi đau khổ trước mắt,
và ta thấy rõ điều này trong việc giảm cân hay kiếm tiền nhiều hơn.
Khi ta cố gắng giảm cân,
tâm trí không chú ý đến nỗi đau về lâu dài mà sự tăng cân gây ra cho cơ thể,
mà nó chỉ quan tâm đến nỗi đau trước mắt của việc phải đoạn tuyệt với chất béo, chất đường.
Cơ thể dần trở nên quen với việc dung nạp nhiều calo.
Nó bắt đầu quen với việc tiêu thụ chất béo, chất đường.
Nhưng đó không phải chỉ là một thói nghiện thôi.
Cơ thể còn sử dụng thức ăn như một cách trốn tránh.
Đây là một hoạt động làm tê liệt cảm xúc được sử dụng như một cơ chế tự vệ khi đối phó với sự xung đột, giằng xé nội tâm.
Tâm trí nghĩ nó làm thế để tránh đau khổ,
nhưng nó chỉ tập trung vào nỗi đau trước mắt để có được niềm vui, cảm giác thỏa mãn tức thời.
Đương nhiên, ta dễ dàng nhận ra sự né tránh nỗi đau đớn trước mắt gây trở ngại cho ta ra sao khi ta sử dụng những hợp chất bên ngoài, nhưng với các khao khát, mong muốn nội tâm thì sao?
Khi ta muốn kiếm nhiều tiền hơn, bạn có nghĩ tất cả chúng ta sẽ bước ra, cố gắng và cố gắng cho đến khi kiếm được nhiều tiền hơn không?
Không, đương nhiên là không.
Tâm trí muốn ta có nhiều tiền hơn, nhưng nó không nhất thiết phải trải qua nhiều đau đớn, khổ sở để có được số tiền ấy.
Nhưng đó là những gì ta cần trải qua khi muốn đạt được cái gì đấy lớn lao, như kiếm được một số tiền khổng lồ hay giảm được một lượng cân nặng đáng kể.
Chắc chắn, bạn phải hy sinh không chỉ thời gian thôi, mà tất cả những gì thuộc bản thân mình.
Nhưng đây chính là lý do tại sao các phương pháp làm giàu nhanh chóng lại dễ dàng đánh lừa được hầu hết mọi người.
Đó là vì tâm trí muốn cái nó muốn, nhưng biết rằng nó phải hoạt động theo nguyên lý hiện thực.
Nguyên lý hiện thực nói rằng bản ngã sẽ cho ta cái ta muốn bên trong giới hạn của thực tế.
Bản ngã sẽ chen vào giữa sức mạnh của id với siêu ngã bằng cách áp dụng nguyên lý hiện thực.
Nhưng khi một phương pháp làm giàu nhanh có vẻ hữu hiệu đến nỗi nó trông giống thật, bản ngã sẽ cho phép ta đi theo nó.
Ta thất bại khi cố tìm xem mình sẽ phải làm gì để kiếm được nhiều tiền hơn.
Khi tìm kiếm một giải pháp nhanh chóng cho các vấn đề tài chính,
ta thường tiếp cận mọi thứ với tầm nhìn bị che khuất.
Và điều này không chỉ ảnh hưởng đến vài người thôi.
Nó khá phổ biến vì nó là sản phẩm của tâm lý tiềm thức.
Bộ máy tâm thần thường đẩy ta về phía những lời mời mọc quá hấp dẫn đến khó tin.
Dù là chế độ ăn kiêng theo mốt, phương pháp làm giàu nhanh chóng, hay bất cứ thứ gì khác,
nếu nó có vẻ quá hiệu quả đến khó tin, thì nó thường không có tác dụng lâu dài.
Nhưng bản ngã không nghĩ như thế.
Khi áp dụng các trào lưu hay phương pháp kiểu này, ta cảm nhận được hiệu ứng trấn an tức thì.
Nhưng đó là kết quả của sự xoa dịu một số áp lực nội tâm.
Tuy nhiên, mọi chuyện không dừng lại ở đó.
Vấn đề là hầu hết mọi người đều muốn chọn cách dễ dàng.
Ta không muốn cứ phải làm việc vất vả, cực nhọc hay đổ mồ hôi sôi nước mắt để đạt được ước mơ, hy vọng.
Ta muốn cái mình muốn và muốn nó ngay lập tức.
Khi thực hiện mục tiêu, ta nhanh chóng bỏ cuộc chỉ vì một thất bại nhỏ.
Khi gặp trở ngại, ta dễ dàng buông xuôi, đầu hàng.
Nhưng trong cuộc sống, cái có giá trị thì khó đạt được.
Bạn sẽ thất bại nhiều lần trước khi thành công.
Sự khác biệt giữa người thành công với người không thành công là người thành công không bỏ cuộc.
Bất kể người hướng về thành công gặp thất bại bao nhiêu lần đi nữa, họ vẫn luôn đứng dậy bước tiếp.
Họ thay đổi, điều chỉnh phương pháp và tiếp tục cố gắng.
Đây là một phần của nghệ thuật kiên trì.
Việc chịu đựng thất bại không quá khó, nhưng chính nỗi sợ thất bại làm tê liệt ta.
Bạn có thể chịu đựng được thất bại, có lẽ bạn từng làm thế trong cuộc đời mình.
Thất bại là dấu hiệu của sự sống.
Nó là dấu hiệu cho thấy bạn đang cố gắng.
Bạn phải tiếp tục kiên trì dù cho có điều gì xảy ra đi nữa.
Nếu bạn hỏi Gandhi hay Martin Luther King, giả sử họ sống ở thời đại này,
rằng họ có chấp nhận thất bại không,
họ sẽ nói đây là câu hỏi lố bịch.
Họ khát khao tự do.
Một người muốn chấm dứt sự cai trị của người Anh,
còn người kia muốn chấm dứt sự áp bức của người da trắng.
Họ chắc chắn đã áp dụng luật hấp dẫn,
vì họ luôn tập trung vào mục tiêu ấy trong tâm trí và không hề nản chí, chùn bước.
Họ hoàn thành mục tiêu bằng cách kiên trì hành động mỗi ngày.
Ngay cả khi thất bại hay đối mặt với nghịch cảnh, họ vẫn tiếp tục cố gắng.
Dù người của họ bị bỏ tù, bắt bớ, tra tấn, hành hạ, bị giết chết, họ vẫn tiếp tục đấu tranh.
Dù làm gì đi nữa, bạn cũng sẽ gặp thất bại.
Càng gặp thất bại nhiều, bạn càng đến gần hơn với mục tiêu.
Nếu bạn hỏi những người thành công nhất trên thế giới bí quyết thành công của họ là gì,
câu trả lời sẽ rất đơn giản.
Sự kiên trì chính là bí quyết thành công.
Nhưng không phải chỉ là sự kiên trì không thôi,
mà là sự kết hợp giữa sự kiên trì với ý nghĩ tích cực cùng hành động.
Bạn phải tiếp tục cố gắng thực hiện mục tiêu,
ngay cả sau khi thất bại, và thay đổi phương pháp nếu cần.
Nếu bạn thất bại, đó là bình thường.
Ngẫm nghĩ lại xem bạn đã làm điều gì sai.
Cố gắng quan sát mọi thứ với một nhận thức mới để biết mình cần thay đổi phương pháp ra sao.
Nếu bạn hỏi một người mẹ đang quan sát con họ tập đi lần đầu tiên rằng
liệu họ có sợ nó sẽ không thể đi được vì thấy nó cứ ngã hết lần này đến lần khác,
họ sẽ nhìn bạn như thể bạn từ trên trời rơi xuống.
Họ sẽ nói bất kể con họ có ngã bao nhiêu lần đi nữa, nó sẽ đi được.
Đứa bé đang tập đi cũng sẽ không ngừng cố gắng.
Nó sẽ thay đổi phương pháp giữ thăng bằng cho đến khi thành công.
Giống như đứa trẻ mới tập đi hay tập nói lần đầu tiên, ta phải kiên trì với các mục tiêu của mình.
Ngay khi ý nghĩ mình sẽ không đạt được cái gì đó xuất hiện trong tâm trí ta, mọi thứ sẽ bắt đầu trượt dốc từ đấy.
Khi có cảm giác mình không thể đạt được cái gì đó, ta sẽ di chuyển về phía của thất bại vì tâm trí sẽ nhận được cái nó tập trung vào.
Tuy nhiên, nếu tâm trí tin rằng ta sẽ thành công dù gặp thất bại bao nhiêu lần đi nữa, ta sẽ di chuyển về phía thành công.
Sức mạnh của sự tập trung suy nghĩ lớn vô cùng.
Nó có thể thôi thúc ta đạt được bất cứ thứ gì.
Vào năm 1940, chỉ cần bạn hỏi bất kỳ ai về khả năng du hành vũ trụ, chứ chưa nói đến việc đưa người lên mặt trăng, họ sẽ nghĩ bạn bị điên.
Nhưng như bạn thấy, mọi thứ ngày nay đã khác vì sức mạnh của sự tập trung suy nghĩ đã giúp ta có nhận thức mới về cái mà ta từng nghĩ là không thể xảy ra.
Cái được coi là khoa học viễn tưởng không lâu trước đây giờ đã trở thành hiện thực.
Liệu bạn dám nói với mọi người ở năm 1940 là họ sẽ có thể giao tiếp, chia sẻ hình ảnh, phim, tin nhắn tức thời qua mạng lưới được liên kết với nhau được gọi là internet không?
Họ sẽ nhìn bạn như thể bạn là kẻ mất trí, điên rồ vậy.
Tất cả những gì ta có hiện nay không chỉ là sản phẩm của các ý nghĩ tích cực, mà còn là sản phẩm của vô số thất bại nữa.
Chính nhờ thất bại mà ta mới đạt được những thứ mà ta có trong cuộc sống của mình hôm nay.
Trong lịch sử, không một thành tựu lớn lao nào chưa từng nếm trải qua thất bại.
Chính từ thất bại mà thành tựu được tạo thành.
Khi có ý nghĩ tích cực rằng mình sẽ đạt được cái gì đó và luôn cố gắng, kiên trì đi về phía nó, ta sẽ thành công.
Chắc chắn, trên đường đi, ta sẽ gặp không ít thất bại.
Càng thất bại nhiều, ta càng đến gần hơn với mục tiêu.
Thất bại không phải là cái gì đấy đáng sợ, mà là cái ta nên đón nhận, vì nếu không có nó, ta sẽ không được như bây giờ.
Đừng sợ thất bại.
Đừng sợ những điều mọi người nghĩ về bạn nếu bạn thất bại.
Hãy tập trung vào mục tiêu cuối, đứng dậy, rồi tiếp tục cố gắng.
Cứ tiếp tục cố gắng cũng như kiên trì cho đến khi bạn hoàn thành được mọi mục tiêu.

title: Chapter 16.
en: +IGNORANCE IS BLISS
"Ignorance is the curse of God; knowledge is the wing wherewith we fly to heaven."
- William Shakespeare.
Oliver sat in the doctor's office, his legs hanging off the examination table as he sat hunched over waiting for the doctor to arrive for his annual physical.
He truly hated something about being there.
Every single time he arrived at Doctor Graham's office in the center of town, he felt sick to his stomach.
He wasn't quite sure what it was about being there,
but he just didn't like it.
The placed smelled like sickness.
That was what he had associated it to be for him.
At 57 years old, Oliver had had his fair share of run-ins with Doctor Graham.
There was the mild stroke he had suffered three years back;
there was the triple bypass surgery when he had hit the big 5-0;
and, there was of course his wife's death.

It was only a little over a year ago that he arrived in that very same office with his wife, who had been feeling perfectly fine just a month before, only to later be notified that she was in the late stages of pancreatic cancer.
She was able to put up a fight at first,
but when the jaundice set in, they knew it was all over.
So, Oliver didn't really like sitting in that doctor's office.
All he could think about was the bad experiences he had suffered there.
But now he was back again.
And, as much as he tried to put his mind off it, the thoughts kept coming back.
His mind kept circling around the negative associations he had with Doctor Graham's office.
And, just as he was submerged in a tirade of thoughts that swept him under the current of negativity, Doctor Graham walked into the room.
He looked at Oliver and exchanged a rare set of glances with him.
Oliver knew just what the doctor was thinking.
It was as if he could read the doctor's mind.
He knew his case was a sympathetic one;
he knew just how low his life had sunk.
And, now he was right back there again in his office,
the same building he had cried his eyes out over his wife not too long ago.
It was only a few feet away, in the doctor's private office, where he had wept uncontrollably.
But, those days were behind him now and he tried to put it off.
He tried not to think of all the hurt and the defeat he had experienced.
It didn't serve Oliver;
none of those feelings served him.
He looked down at the floor after exchanging pleasantries with the doctor and watched as he made notations on his chart.
He would ask Oliver questions from time to time, just to see his response.
Oliver was sure that the doctor already knew the answer to many of the questions he was asking,
but he asked them anyhow.
He wasn't quite sure if this was something that all doctors did, but he went along with it.
All the while, as Oliver was answering the doctor's questions, almost autonomously,
he looked down and stared at his feet.
He looked carefully at his toes,
realizing just how strange it felt to be sitting there hunched over and staring at them.
He couldn't remember the last time he really stared at his toes,
and he was once again entrenched in thoughts that seemed to take him on a wild journey.
What was he doing there?
Why did he even come to the doctor's office again when he hated it so much?
He kept spinning in his sea of negativity until the doctor snapped him out of it again.
He began asking him questions about his health.
Particularly, he was interested in his cigarette smoking.
Oliver had smoked for much of his life.
He had never thought much about it
until the recent couple of years when his smoking habit had worsened.
Sometimes, he would catch himself smoking a cigarette and forget that he had even lit it in the first place.
It was so ingrained in him that the behavior was virtually unconscious
until the cigarette hit his lips and the smoke was halfway down his throat and entering his lungs.
He didn't want to talk about his cigarette smoking,
but that's what the doctor wanted to talk about.
Not again, he thought.
It was his only vice left.
And, as the doctor began to ask him more questions,
Oliver began revealing the severity of his addiction.
His two-pack-a-day habit had climbed to four packs per day just before his wife had died.
In fact, Oliver was chainsmoking during parts of the day.
He didn't feel like he wanted to be without a cigarette in his mouth.
And, those cigarettes helped him.
They helped him cope with all of the emotional fallout and anguish that he had suffered.
He wanted nothing more than to be able to just continue to smoke.
So, what was Oliver supposed to do?
Was he supposed to just up and stop smoking?
The doctor had asked him about his bad habit in the past,
but he hadn't pressed Oliver.
He hadn't pressed Oliver because he knew what he had gone through.
But, after a mild stroke and triple bypass surgery,
the doctor felt that Oliver should have known better.
Albeit, since the death of his wife, Oliver seemed to care less and less about his own health; at least on the outside that's how he felt.
He didn't really think too much about his own health anymore;
he didn't feel like his own health was even that important.
In fact, Oliver had let himself go in many ways;
the cigarette smoking wasn't the only big problem he was facing.
Oliver was also eating like it was going out of style.
In the past year, Oliver had put on nearly fifty pounds.
Now, Oliver's weight wasn't the major concern for the doctor,
but his cigarette smoking was.
And, if the doctor didn't try to help intervene now,
they could all spiral out of control soon.
As the doctor grilled Oliver about the cigarette smoking, he felt worse and worse.
Sure, he had been experiencing some odd problems lately that included a very raspy cough, wheeziness in his chest, and a few other complications.
He knew that it was going to be a difficult visit.
He knew that the doctor was going to scold him for not taking better care of his health.
But, Oliver didn't really think he cared that much.
He didn't think he had that much to look forward to anymore.
He used to look at life as one beautiful gift, but then everything changed.
His whole world was flipped upside down in one fell swoop.
It was as if his worst nightmares had come true.
It was as if he was living a nightmare and he didn't know what to do anymore.
So, he just continued to smoke.
He continued on that tirade of addictive behavior because nothing else soothed his nerves, and nothing else helped him to escape from the chaotic world that was known as his life.
He didn't know just how to explain it to the doctor.
As much as he tried, he just kept coming up with blank stares.
It wasn't until the doctor asked Oliver some more questions - some serious questions
- that his demeanor suddenly took on a more serious tone.
Oliver had seen this side of Doctor Graham before.
He knew just what the doctor looked like when he was about to dish out some news that wasn't going to be received in the best manner by the opposing party.
He braced himself for what was to come.
He didn't know if he was going to be able to take it, but he knew he was there for a reason.
He knew he had to hear the doctor out no matter what.
There was nowhere for him to hide.
He couldn't run off somewhere and just hide away;
he knew he couldn't do that.
Whatever it was, he was just going to grit and bear it.
He was going to take whatever was thrown his way.
And, besides, he didn't really care anymore about his life, right?
He didn't really care what the doctor had to say.
And, really, what could it be?
How bad could it actually be?
How much worse could his life actually look at that point?
These questions ran through his head as he looked up at the doctor,
and then back down at his toes again.
But, there was a problem with Oliver's lungs.
Something was wrong, and it was serious.
The doctor went into detail about a potential problem with something he had spotted an anomaly on one of his exams.
It was clear that he had been smoking too much, but now what?
Was it what he had dreaded it might be?
Was it really cancer?
Oliver couldn't look the doctor in the eyes as he began explaining to him the potential for what it might be.
It could be a malignant tumor.
It could be life threatening.
The x-ray wasn't conclusive enough.
They had to do more tests.
The doctor scheduled Oliver for a CAT scan the following week,
and as Oliver drove home that day, he could only dread the worst situation.
He could only think about how bad his life had become.
He pictured dying in his mind.
He pictured his last days on earth.
But that was what he wanted, wasn't it?
Didn't he want to die?
He thought about it all on his drive home.
It was the longest drive he had taken in his entire life.
Did he really want to die?
Did he really want to leave the earth and be without his children?
Didn't he want to see his daughter have her first child or his son graduate from college?
No, Oliver didn't want to die.
When he broke the news to family and friends, they were devastated.
Oliver couldn't even look at cigarettes during this period.
He couldn't even stand the look of those slender sticks that were ruining his life.
He didn't have an escape anymore.
All he could do was think,
and that's all that Oliver did for the week.
All he could think about was how he had gotten to where he was.
How did it all get so bad?
How did his bad habits bring him to that present-day situation?
He had so many questions in his mind,
but during this time, he also began to loathe cigarettes.
He began to research just what those cigarettes had been doing to his body.
And, in the days leading up to the CAT scan, he lived in a constant state of fear.
His nerves were frayed, and he simply couldn't concentrate on anything else.
How could he?
How could he think about absolutely anything else when all he could think about was dying?
Sure, when his wife died, he could think of nothing more than of joining her,
but he later realized that she would have wanted him to live.
Now was it his time as well?
Was it time to go?
The week dragged on uncomfortably slowly.
It was the slowest week of his entire life.
The fear of not knowing was eating away at him.
But, because of that week, Oliver threw out every cigarette he could find in his possession.
He made a vow to himself that, if he made it through this thing, that he would never smoke again.
He wanted to live, and the cigarettes were killing him.
They were what had brought him to that situation.
The doctor had warned him many times in the past, but Oliver felt like he was invincible.
He felt like nothing could go wrong with his own health.
And, when his wife died, he simply didn't care.
But, realizing it now, Oliver did care.
He wanted to see his daughter have a child;
he wanted to be a grandfather.
He wanted to see his only son graduate from college;
he really did.
These were the simple pleasures in life that he had all but forgotten.
He had become so fixated on the problems in his own life that he hadn't stopped to open his eyes and appreciate all that he had that was positive in his life.
He felt so awful for living his life that way for so many years.
It was as if he had been in a trance and now he had been awakened.
When he arrived for the CAT scan, Oliver was filled with anxious nerves.
But, he had never felt so clear about what he wanted in his entire life.
As he sat there during the procedure, he prayed and prayed that everything would be all right.
He made a promise to God that if he were meant to live, he would make a difference in the world.
He would stop fixating on the negative and he would do something positive.
The feeling was so cathartic that, as the scan was being completed, Oliver felt as though his soul had been cleansed.
He felt like, no matter what had happened, it would be all right.
Whatever was meant to be would be.
He was going to stop worrying about it.
And, a couple of days later, as he was seated with Doctor Graham back in his office, he received the news he was hoping to hear.
It was a benign tumor.
But, the doctor warned him about his health and his smoking.
He told Oliver that if he continued down this path, it could end very terribly for him.
However, Oliver didn't need the pep talk.
He didn't need the doctor to tell him just how bad things could turn out.
That week, he got a glimpse of what life could be like when he knew it was ending.
He didn't want it to end.
His health was that important to him.
He had a reason why he needed to break his bad habits.
That was all the motivation he had needed.
But, it was unfortunate that it took a nearly catastrophic experience for him to snap himself out of his old ways.
And, as he sat there speaking to the doctor,
he explained to him just how much of an internal transformation he had gone through that week.
He explained just how he had felt before, and how he felt now.
It was as if he had a renewed sense of spirit.
He didn't want to live an unhappy and unhealthy life anymore;
he wanted to be free.
When the doctor heard this from Oliver, he became very pleased.
He was happy that something good had come out of a potentially bad situation.
And, he was happy that the streak of bad luck had ended for Oliver.
It had been one time too many that he had to deliver the bad news to Oliver
and watch as he broke down in front of him.
On the way home from the doctor's office that day, Oliver was happier than he could ever remember being before in his life.
Something had changed about him.
He was an entirely different person.
It was as if the week he spent fretting over the likelihood of his death and what he was going to miss out on in life, had completely changed his way of thinking.
He realized he had had so much to live for.
He realized that there was a reason why he needed to improve his health;
there was a strong enough reason to stop smoking.
And, although Oliver had tried to quit in the past, he knew this would be different.
And, as the months and years rolled on,
friends and family members couldn't stop commenting on just how much Oliver had changed.
He was living a clean and healthy life that was no longer cluttered with unnecessary toxins and distractions.
He became an inspiration to those around him.
He had a chance to witness his first granddaughter being brought into this world and his son graduating from college.
He looked at the gleam in their eyes and thanked the Lord for sparing his life.
Before all of this, he was unable to see how his poor beliefs were leading to poor decisions,
but not anymore.
That was all over now.
Everything was different now.
Everything.
Oftentimes in life, we choose not to see what we don't believe in.
Whether it's political in nature, religious, racial, or financial,
our present-day experiences are filtered through the lens of our beliefs.
When our beliefs support a certain point-of-view,
then we're readily able to see more examples that support that viewpoint.
It's similar to the example of purchasing a new or used car.
Prior to obtaining that vehicle, your mind wasn't trained to see it on the roads,
but afterwards, it sees it everywhere.
It's not because the car suddenly started to show up everywhere once you purchased it,
but rather that the mind's eye became trained to see it once the vehicle was acquired.
This example is very similar to how our beliefs filter the experiences in the world.
When we choose to believe a certain way, we only see those things that support that belief.
So, it goes without saying then that, no matter what we believe in, we'll get more of it.
Or, rather, whatever we focus on, we'll attract more of.
This comes back to the conversation on thoughts,
and how- no matter what we focus on, we'll attract more of that into our lives.
When we focus on negativity, we attract more negativity.
But, should we choose to focus on positivity,
we'll attract more positivity into our lives.
There's something visceral about the vibrational energy created with our thoughts.
These vibrational energies send out thought wavelengths that signal other interconnected beings.
Whether a person likes it or not, others can sense this vibrational energy
and it will either attract or repel them depending on their own vibrational energy.
Imagine, for example, the woman or man who exudes sexual energy.
Sexual energy is very high on the spectrum of powerful vibrational energies because it's a basal instinct in all organisms.
When a person exudes sexual energy,
whether they are dressed the part or not, the signals can be received loud and clear.
Similarly, when a person exudes a very depressed or angry energy,
these can be picked up by others as well.
Most people don't realize just how much others are picking up their vibrational energies.
It's difficult to notice when we're going about our days, full engrossed in our lives, to see just how clear of a message we're giving off.
But, if you've ever come across an energy that's somewhat akin to yours,
have you never felt drawn to it?
That's because like energies will attract other like energies
- angry people are attracted to other people that are angry,
just as much as happy people are attracted to other people that are happy.
So, if this is the case, why don't more of us change our focus so that we move in a more positive direction?
Why can't we seem to create that internal shift that's necessary for us to move beyond our present-day limitations?
Well, it has a lot to do with our conditioning.
Our minds become so accustomed to a way of thinking that, in order for it to see anything else, becomes remarkably difficult.
And, ignorance truly becomes bliss.
It's difficult for the mind to notice anything outside the realm of its known possibilities.
It's difficult for it to see beyond that which it already knows.
It chooses to acknowledge what exists,
but doesn't wholeheartedly agree with it;
it chooses to ignore the truths that are external to it.
Due to this very severely debilitating factor of the human mind, progress becomes remarkably difficult to achieve.
It becomes virtually impossible to move outside the boundaries of what's already known to the human mind when it doesn't have other external references to base its experiences off.
That's why it's important to surround yourself with people that are already living the life of your dreams, because the mind moves towards that which it focuses on.
And, when you do this, the mind sees the external references right there in front of it.
The mind can see the realm of possibility when it's right there staring it in the face.
When others around you are already living the life of your dreams, it's not so difficult of a leap for the mind to make.
Things become much more real, and the mind has more difficulty ignoring the realm of possibility when it's right there in front of it.
There's an internal shift that occurs from a state of "I think it's possible," to "I know it's possible." And this is incredibly powerful.
It can make all the difference between the desire to achieve and the ability to follow through and realize one's dreams.
But, it's easy to ignore what's within the realm of possibility.
When we're so caught up in our lives and what's going on,
it's easy to forget what we can achieve.
The mind constantly exists in a state that dwells on the past and frets over the future,
that it rarely recognizes the potential of unlimited possibility that exists.
It turns on its critical and judgmental engines from the moment we awake until the moment that we go to sleep.
This makes it hard to focus on the realm of possibility when it's so worried about the realm of negativity.
It's hard to see past one's struggles at times without some points of reference.
That's why it's important to surround yourself with positive references and a general set of positive influences
that can drive the mind in the right overall direction.
When the mind is weighed down by negative influences,
it's difficult for it to move beyond the negativity.
When people who constantly try to keep you down surround you,
it's difficult for the mind to overcome this barrier to foster positivity.
And, ignorance truly is bliss
when we're talking about the state-of-mind that we have when life's negativity surrounds us.
The mind prefers not to know about the realm of possibility because it would cause us too much pain.
We seek comfort in that which we already know.
If we only know sickness, poverty, or anger,
then we seek comfort in finding that in our lives
and we attract it to us.
The mind is going to attract that which it focuses on,
and negativity will breed more negativity.
The mind will choose to ignore what it doesn't know.
If the mind only knows about lack and poverty,
it will choose to ignore abundance and wealth.
The mind will ignore these things because it does more to avoid pain than it does to gain pleasure.
Knowing about abundance and wealth when we're living in a state of lack and poverty can cause too much pain to the mind.
It's too much pain because the mind knows just how large of a hurdle it is to overcome its present-day obstacles to achieve abundance and wealth,
so it chooses to ignore it.
That's why the mind will seek out what it knows.
It's your duty to forcibly change what the mind focuses on, and thus seeks out.
This is why the chapters on thought and the law of attraction in this book are so important when it comes to shaping your destiny.
If you can't adhere to the principles and teachings in these chapters, then it's remarkably difficult to overcome the seemingly insurmountable in life.
You must change your focus entirely, have a strong enough reason why you must achieve something, and persistently act towards it.
You can't allow the mind to wallow only in a state of what it knows.
It has to be actively trained to excel for much more in life.
The mind, like an Olympic Athlete, has to train itself to be prepared for leading an excellent life.
If the mind is constantly weighed down, not only by negative influences, but also by toxins entering it on a regular basis, the difficulty for it to overcome obstacles increases exponentially.
Train the mind, not to ignore that which it doesn't know, but rather to embrace it.
It has to embrace what it doesn't know and expect that it is possible, because anything is possible.
Anything that the mind can constantly focus on and persistently act towards is possible to achieve.
+THE 4-MINUTE MILE
For hundreds of years, people were fixated on breaking the 4-minute mile.
People wanted to run a mile in under four minutes, but simply were unable to.
They attributed this to a limit in human performance and came up with a variety of excuses.
But, this didn't stop athletes from pushing towards this very elusive singular goal.
It wasn't until the year 1900 when man started to get close with a mile run at 4 minutes and 15 seconds.
Then, in 1923, it was 4 minutes and 10 seconds.
In the 1930's, the record was down to 4 minutes and 6 seconds, and to 4 minutes and 1 second in the 1940's.
Finally, in 1954, Roger Bannister broke the 4- minute mile, running it in 3 minutes and 59 seconds (3:59.4).
But, before Roger Bannister broke the 4-minute mile, no other person was able to do so.
Was this just a frame-of-mind?
Clearly, the human body didn't have the physical limitations of not being able to break the 4-minute mile,
so what changed?
Well, as you can see, as time progressed, man inched closer and closer to his goal of a 4-minute mile.
From 1900 to the 1940's, the record came down to just a hair away from it at 4 minutes and 1 second.
So, the frame of reference started changing.
Man realized that it was quite possible, with persistence, to achieve that goal.
But it wasn't going to be easy.
The goal was founded not only on the positive thoughts and expectations of achieving the goal, but also a strong enough reason why a person had to achieve that goal.
But it wasn't just the thoughts; it was the persistent focused action on those thoughts.
Roger Bannister moved closer and closer to that goal until he finally broke that record.
Then, almost immediately after Roger Bannister's record-breaking run, John Landy broke the 4-minute mile just 46 days after Bannister.
So, how was it that for hundreds of years man couldn't break the record of a 4-minute mile, and then within just 46 days of one another, 2 men break the record?
Well, the frame of reference changed once again, but this time much more dramatically.
Once one person broke the record, the realm of possibility opened up.
People now knew it was possible to break the record.
When something goes from a possibility to a known accomplishment, a dramatic shift occurs in the human mind.
That's because the human mind founds itself on beliefs.
If it believes that it can accomplish something, then it can.
And, there's nothing stronger as a belief than the actual achievement of a particular goal by another individual.
When the mind realizes that another person was able to achieve something, then it knows that it can achieve it as well.
It doesn't become a maybe anymore; it becomes a certainty for achievement.
It puts the goal much closer within reach when it knows that someone else was able to achieve it.
After Landy broke the 4-minute mile, 3 others were also able to break it within one year.
So, within 13 months of Bannister's record, 4 other athletes had broken the 4-minute mile.
This is after an extraordinary amount of effort put out by individuals trying to break the record.
And, within 5 years of Bannister's record, 21 total athletes had broken the record.
The realm of possibility shifted and it was a dramatic shift.
This moves out of a state of ignorance by the mind, especially when the mind knoxvs that something is achievable.
But, the mind must be trained to look at the right references.
This is especially true for the person, organization, company, or country trying to achieve the yet unachieved goal, such as before landing a man on the moon, or before the abolition of slavery.
The list can go on and on here, but it's safe to say that the mind will see that which it focuses on.
However, the mind will also easily ignore references when it feels like achieving something is going to bring too much pain.

When it feels like it's going to have to step too far out of its comfort zone, and potentially experience a lot of heartache and struggle to achieve or accomplish something, it's going to reject the notion.
The mind is going to want to revert back to the pleasure-driven pursuits once it realizes just how difficult it's going to be to attain something it once thought was much more easily attainable.
Unfortunately, this is part of the inner workings of our minds.
The psychic apparatus - the ego, the id, and the superego - reign supreme, and without complete awareness of the processes in your mind, it's quite difficult to make lasting improvements.
The pleasure-seeking pursuits of the id are always going to trump the realistic expectations and nose-to-the-grindstone that comes with long-term achievement.
The psychic apparatus is going to default us to take the easy way out all the time.
That's because it wants to give us what we want now, but within reality.
However, oftentimes it's not willing to endure years of heartache and struggle in order for us to achieve something.
That's because the id is too powerful in our minds.
But, if this one single process can be overridden with awareness and constant persistent action, we can move closer and closer each day to our goals.
And, the references are everywhere.
Just like with the individuals who ran a 4-minute mile, people have achieved so much in life.
It's important to seek those people out and learn about their struggles.
Find out what they did to achieve the life you're looking to lead.
It doesn't take a lot of work to find them, just some persistent searching and digging.

Họ muốn chạy một dặm dưới bốn phút, nhưng không thể làm được.
Họ coi đây là giới hạn của con người và đưa ra rất nhiều lý do.
Nhưng điều này không ngăn cản được các vận động viên ngừng cố gắng theo đuổi mục tiêu không tưởng này.
Năm 1900, con người bắt đầu đến gần với mục tiêu ấy, chạy được một dặm trong 4 phút 15 giây.
Sau đó, đến năm 1923, kỷ lục mới được xác lập là 4 phút 10 giây.
Thập niên 1930, kỷ lục này được phá vỡ xuống còn 4 phút 6 giây, và đến thập niên 1940 là 4 phút 1 giây.
Cuối cùng, vào năm 1954, Roger Bannister đã phá giới hạn chạy một dặm trong bốn phút, xác lập kỷ lục mới là 3 phút 59 giây (3:59.4).
Nhưng trước khi Roger phá vỡ giới hạn này, không người nào khác có thể làm được điều ấy.
Điều này có phụ thuộc vào trạng thái tinh thần không?
Rõ ràng, cơ thể con người không có hạn chế về mặt sức khỏe để không thể phá vỡ giới hạn chạy một dặm trong bốn phút.
Vậy điều gì đã thay đổi?
Như bạn thấy, thời gian trôi qua, con người càng lúc càng đến gần hơn mục tiêu chạy một dặm trong bốn phút.
Từ năm 1900 đến thập niên 1940, kỷ lục đã từ từ giảm dần xuống còn 4 phút 1 giây.
Như vậy có nghĩa là trạng thái tinh thần bắt đầu thay đổi.
Con người nhận ra rằng chỉ cần kiên trì, họ có thể phá được kỷ lục này.
Nhưng mọi chuyện sẽ không dễ dàng như thế.
Để đạt được mục tiêu, một người không chỉ cần có ý nghĩ tích cực cùng niềm hy vọng sẽ đạt được nó, mà họ còn phải có lý do đủ mạnh giải thích được tại sao mình phải đạt được nó.
Ngoài ra, người ấy phải có hành động kiên trì với các ý nghĩ tích cực.
Roger Bannister kiên trì theo đuổi mục tiêu cho đến khi hoàn thành nó.
Sau khi Roger Bannister thiết lập kỷ lục chạy mới được 46 ngày, John Landy cũng phá vỡ giới hạn chạy một dặm trong bốn phút.
Vậy tại sao suốt hàng trăm năm trời, con người không thể phá vỡ được giới hạn này, trong khi chỉ trong vòng 46 ngày, có đến 2 người vượt qua được nó?
Trạng thái tinh thần lại thay đổi một lần nữa, nhưng lần này nó thay đổi nhanh hơn.
Khi một người phá vỡ được kỷ lục, khả năng mở ra.
Mọi người biết kỷ lục nào cũng có thể bị phá vỡ.
Khi cái gì đó chuyển từ trạng thái có thể sang khả năng chắc chắn hơn, sự thay đổi đột ngột sẽ xuất hiện trong tâm trí con người.
Đó là vì nền tảng của tâm trí là niềm tin.
Nếu nó tin rằng mình sẽ đạt được cái gì đó, thì nó sẽ đạt được cái đó.
Và nói đến niềm tin, không gì có tính thuyết phục hơn thành công thật sự của một người với một mục tiêu cụ thể.
Khi tâm trí nhận thấy người khác đạt được cái gì đó, nó biết mình cũng có thể đạt được cái ấy.
Bây giờ, mục tiêu không phải là cái có thể đạt được nữa, mà nó sẽ là cái chắc chắn đạt được.
Khi tâm trí biết một người khác đạt được mục tiêu, nó sẽ kéo mục tiêu vào bên trong tầm với của mình.
Sau khi Landy vượt qua giới hạn chạy một dặm trong bốn phút, ba người khác cũng vượt qua được nó chỉ trong vòng một năm.
Như vậy, trong vòng 13 tháng sau khi Bannister xác lập kỷ lục mới, 4 vận động viên khác cũng vượt qua giới hạn chạy một dặm trong bốn phút.
Để làm được điều này, họ đã nỗ lực rất nhiều.
Trong vòng 5 năm sau khi Bannister thiết lập kỷ lục mới, có cả thảy 21 vận động viên đã vượt qua khỏi giới hạn ấy.
Nhận thức của tâm trí về khả năng thay đổi, và đó là sự thay đổi lớn.
Tâm trí thoát khỏi giới hạn không biết của nó, nhất là khi nó biết rằng cái gì đó có thể đạt được.
Nhưng tâm trí phải được huấn luyện để hướng vào mục tiêu đúng đắn.
Điều này đặc biệt đúng với một người, tổ chức, công ty, hay đất nước đang cố gắng hoàn thành mục tiêu tưởng chừng không thể đạt được như đưa người lên mặt trăng, hay bãi bỏ chế độ nô lệ.
Ta có thể liệt kê thêm nhiều mục tiêu khác, nhưng nói gì thì nói, tâm trí sẽ nhìn thấy cái nó tập trung vào.
Tuy nhiên, tâm trí cũng dễ dàng phớt lờ một khả năng khi nó cảm thấy việc đạt được cái gì đó sẽ đem lại nhiều đau đớn, khổ sở cho mình.
Khi nó cảm thấy nó sẽ phải đi quá xa ra khỏi vùng an toàn của mình, và sẽ trải nghiệm nhiều đau khổ cùng khó khăn mới đạt được cái gì đó, nó sẽ bỏ ý niệm ấy.
Tâm trí sẽ muốn quay lại với các nhu cầu muốn được thỏa mãn tức thời khi nó nhận ra việc đạt được cái mà nó từng nghĩ là sẽ dễ dàng đạt được.
Không may, đây là một phần trong cơ chế hoạt động nội tại của tâm trí.
Bộ máy tâm thần - bản ngã, id, siêu ngã - nắm quyền tối cao, và nếu không có nhận thức đầy đủ về các quá trình trong tâm trí, ta khó mà tạo ra sự tiến bộ, phát triển lâu dài.
Nhu cầu tìm kiếm sự thỏa mãn tức thời của id luôn tìm cách bác bỏ các kỳ vọng thực tế cùng sự nỗ lực không ngừng nghỉ gắn liền với thành công lâu dài.
Bộ máy tâm thần sẽ xúi giục ta chọn cách dễ dàng nhất.
Đó là vì nó muốn cho ta cái ta muốn ngay bây giờ, nhưng trong giới hạn thực tế.
Tuy nhiên, bộ máy tâm thần thường không sẵn sàng chịu đựng hàng năm dài đau đớn, khổ sở, vất vả để giúp ta đạt được cái gì đấy.
Đó là do id quá mạnh trong tâm trí ta.
Nhưng nếu các nhu cầu của id bị chế ngự bởi nhận thức sáng suốt cùng hành động kiên trì, càng ngày ta sẽ càng đến gần với mục tiêu hơn.
Những tấm gương thành công ở khắp mọi nơi.
Giống như người vượt qua được mục tiêu chạy một dặm trong 4 phút, trong cuộc sống có rất nhiều người thành công.
Ta cần tìm kiếm những người này và tìm hiểu về mọi khó khăn, gian khổ mà họ đã trải qua.
Hãy tìm hiểu xem họ đã làm gì để có được cuộc sống mà bạn mơ ước.
Sẽ không khó để tìm ra họ, chỉ cần bạn kiên trì tìm kiếm mà thôi.

title: Chapter 17.
en: +BREAKING BAD HABITS
So much of what holds us back in life are bad habits.
And, as you may have already come to know, bad habits are incredibly hard to break.
They can also be our demise when we try to push past our present-day limitations.
And, those bad habits stem from conditioning that our mind has achieved over the years.
If you're used to walking through your front door, sitting down on the couch, and turning on the television for a multi-hour session in couch-potato land,
then that bad habit may be holding you back from your dreams.
But, how do we break bad habits that we've come to know over the course of our lives?
How do we go from eating foods laden with fat and sugar, to natural, healthy, and organic meals rich in fresh vegetables, fruits, and organic healthy meats?
There's no easy way about it,
because it's incredibly difficult.
Changing the conditioning that the mind and body have become accustomed to takes consistent focused action over an extended period.
But, what is a habit really?
Where do habits come from and how are they formed?
By first understanding how you created your bad habits, you can work to unravel some of the mysteries behind why you do the things that you do.
And, since habits really are routines that are repeated often and occur at the subconscious level, it's important to understand your habits.
If your habits are bad habits, then it's important to build awareness towards them and eliminate them.
Since habits are behaviors that are repeated in a consistent manner on average for approximately 60 to 90 days, they can be difficult to break.
This is especially true when you're dealing with bad habits.
For example, the cigarette smoker that instantly reaches for a cigarette as soon as their meal is complete goes through a ritualistic set of behaviors, which have developed into a habit.
When the meal is complete, the cigarette smoker reaches for their pack of cigarettes and lighter, almost unwittingly.
Once the cigarette is in hand, it's lit, and placed to the mouth.
It almost all happens as part of a subconscious process, especially in cases of individuals who've been smoking for years and years.
So, how do you break these bad habits?

When the American Journal of Psychology described habits in 1903, saying that they are "more or less a fixed way of thinking, willing, or feeling acquired through previous repetition of a mental experience," they understated just how ingrained habits can become.
Of course, back then, we didn't know as much about the human mind as we do today.
But, habits are something that all organisms utilize for shortcuts to routine activities.
And, since those habits form a neural pathway in the neural networks of the brain, rewiring those neural pathways takes a lot of work.
If you want to break your bad habits, you're going to have to arduously rewire your subconscious processes.
So, how is this done?
How do you go about reversing conditioning that has become so akin to your own mind?
How do you unweave what's been woven over the course of years and years of habitual repetition?
As you know, it's not easy to change a habit.
If you've tried to break a bad habit in the past, you know just how difficult it can be.
But it's certainly possible.
Our bad habits can severely limit us and hold us back from attaining the life we want to lead.
When we would rather relax in front of the television instead of putting our nose to the grindstone and making some progress on whatever goal it may be, it can be hard to break those bad habits.
Furthermore, when the habits go not only from mental addictions, but also into physical addictions, breaking free becomes even harder to do.
So, the most important underlying tool you must start with to break a bad habit, is having a strong enough reason why you must break it.
You see, that neural pathway has been etched in your mind so profoundly that the mind is going to take that route almost no matter what you do.
Since it's processing so much of your actions on a subconscious level, as soon as it slips into habit and routine, your willpower will begin to buckle and break.
When the mind switches to these neural pathways, you loose conscious decision-making power unless you build a high degree of awareness towards your actions.
And, even then, it becomes difficult to extricate yourself from these learned behaviors.
So, if you have a strong enough reason why you must break a bad habit, this must be the starting point for improvement.
If a bad habit rests in the way of your goals, and you went through the goal setting section of this book, then you should have your reasons.
If you know why you must accomplish something, and you can see that a bad habit is standing in your way, then for that same reason, you must abolish the bad habit.
Remember, removal of the bad habit is going to take at least 60 to 90 days of new repetitive behavior.
Sometimes, removal of a bad habit can take upwards of 6 months.
But, if you can commit to something for at least 90 days, then you can come very close to surely eliminating a bad habit standing in the way of your hopes and your dreams.
Grab a sheet of paper and jot down the bad habits that have held you back in the past.
Before, when you wanted to accomplish something, what held you back?
What emotion-numbing activities did you slip back into to?
What was that process like when you tried to lose weight and you failed?
Did you end up driving to a fast-food restaurant on your way home from work?
Try to see if you can pinpoint the bad habits and jot them down.
If you're serious about eliminating them from your life, then it's going to take commitment.
Once you have your bad habits listed there on a sheet of paper,
next to them, right down just what goal it has stopped you from achieving in the past.
What has it held you back from doing?
How has it held you back from living the life of your dreams?
Remember, ignorance is bliss,
and when you don't build a degree of conscious awareness to the emotion-numbing activities that are holding you back,
the psychic apparatus can continue to have its way with you.
When you can't see just how much a certain behavior is stopping you from succeeding,
the ego can tip the scales towards the id when the id calls for some pleasure-driven pursuit.
If you've wanted to start your own business in the past,
but you always seem to end up spending your money when you go out with your friends drinking,
then you need to see what the disconnect is there.
If drinking is a bad habit, then it needs to be eliminated.
Many of us cannot moderate certain behavior,
and bad behaviors such as overdrinking, overeating, and overspending can be progressive.
As the neural pathways for those habits build and build, they can reach a higher frequency each time they're engaged in.
When this happens, the emotional highs are higher and the lows are lower.
If you're honest enough in this exercise, then you should be able to see just what bad habits have held you back from your goals in your past.
If you're not honest enough about it, then it may be a bit more difficult.
If you can't see the bad habits that have held you back from your goals in the past, then you may need to ask some friends or family members.
It's always much easier to see the bad habits in people that are close to us, than it is to see our own bad habits.
This, of course, is due to the ego, and the way in which it obscures our own bad habits from us.
When we can't see just how detrimental a certain behavior is, then we don't allow it to cause us enough pain to stop that behavior.
And, since bad habits are learned behaviors that are repeated over an extended period of time, it would cause too much pain for us to try to break a habit that brings us pleasure in the short term.
Remember, the ego is doing more to avoid pain in the short term than it is in the long term.
That's why it's important to shift that paradigm and not allow ignorance to be bliss anymore.
Once you start building awareness towards your habitual behaviors, you can work towards eradicating them from your life.
But, without first being aware of them, you can't work towards eradicating them.
So, if something means enough to you in your life,
you're going to do whatever it takes to accomplish it or get rid of it, in the case of bad habits.
Thus, if you can't attribute a strong enough meaning to something in your life,
then you won't be able to override your natural tendencies.
You won't be able to change behavior that has become so ingrained in you, that's nearly a part of who you are.
Establish a deep enough meaning, and you can do anything.
For example, if you have children, what would you do to protect those children?
What if their lives were in danger and there was something that you could do to save them?
Wouldn't you do just about anything?
Of course, you would;
almost all parents would.
That's because of the meaning that you attribute to their lives and having them happy, healthy, and safe.
You would go to any extents to protect them.
Similarly, if you want to save yourself from whatever detrimental behavior or pathway that you're on,
your future has to be important enough to you.
If you have children, that you care deeply enough about,
then why would you smoke cigarettes that may or may not cause you cancer?
Why would a parent overeat or overspend, causing them physical, emotional, or mental anguish?
Don't children deserve to have parents that are also happy, healthy, and safe?
When you can find a strong enough meaning, you can override your bad habits.
But, without doing this, you won't be able to break those bad patterns in your life.
You might catch yourself doing something only when you're in the midst of it, because it was an autonomous action ingrained in one of your habits.
So, you have to break those bad habits if you're going to accomplish your dreams.
You have to invoke the law of attraction and the power of focused thought here, but you first have to have that strong enough meaning.
On that sheet of paper, write down what you're going to do to break each of those bad habits.
If you're stopping for fast food on your way to work, write out a new planned route that won't drive you by any of those restaurants.
Maybe plan out some healthy snacks to eat along the way that won't leave you feeling starved.
Whatever your bad habits are, you have to do whatever is in your power to break them, or they will continue to break you.
Make it important enough and you can overcome those bad habits.
If you can't attribute an important meaning to them, then they will continue to consume you.
+HAPPINESS, HEALTH, LOVE, AND PROSPERITY
"Happiness doesn't depend on any external conditions, it is governed by our mental attitude."
- Dale Carnegie.
What does it take to succeed in today's competitive environment?
I'm not just talking about monetary success here, but also a state of happiness, health, love, and prosperity across all spectrums.
Unfortunately, when we talk about success, most people instantly become fixated on monetary success, almost entirely forgetting about all other types of success.
But, why should anyone really care about success in the other areas in life when money has become so elevated in society?
Why should anyone want to succeed in other areas in life?
Well, it's because, contrary to popular belief, money can't buy love, happiness, or health.
Money is merely a vehicle for traveling through time and space.
Sure, it may allow you to arrive at your problems in style, but it really can only provide the tangible, and not the intangible.

And, although money is a means to an end when it comes to things like increasing health, opportunities for love, and happiness through the accumulation of goods, it shouldn't be the overall barometer for success.
In the pages of this book, you've gotten a glimpse of what it takes to succeed by utilizing the art of persistence.
But, what you also should have taken away is why you want to succeed.
Why do you want to persist?
Why do you want to attain some level of happiness, health, love, or overall prosperity?
What do those things mean to you?
In life, we can achieve whatever we set our minds to;
this is something that's abundantly clear.
We've seen it happen through the annals of time
- people have set out to achieve lofty goals and have done so.
But, nothing worthwhile is going to come easy,
and everything worth achieving is going to take time.
However, if you've surrounded yourself with negativity,
it's important to remember that you're going to beget more negativity.
It's virtually impossible to achieve something that may seem unreasonable when people around you are holding you back.
When the level of noise is so loud, it's difficult to rise above.
Think back on your life to anything that you've achieved that was worth achieving.
How many people told you that it couldn't be done?
How many people tried to convince you to shy away from those dreams and give them up?
What were all the factors that were working against you?
If you accomplished something notable in your life, then you should take a pause to reflect on that.
You should think about just what obstacles you were able to overcome and how you overcame them.
How did you persist through the struggles?
How did you manage to not give up?
What were the thoughts that were running through your mind?
Any man or woman who can achieve something worthwhile has to have not only a strong enough reason, but also strong enough thoughts to support them.
Their vision has to be grand, but so does the framework of thoughts that make up their lives.
If someone doesn't think they can achieve something, then they'll never be able to do so, no matter how hard they try.
In the past, if you tried to achieve something,
and it didn't mean enough to you,
then you most likely saw yourself giving up.
No matter what a person does,
if a goal isn't important enough to them, then they won't have the mental strength to make it through.
This is why it's so important to come up with a strong enough reason for achieving your goals.
Once you have a strong enough reason,
then you should set about surrounding yourself with enough positive references and thoughts to see you through.
If you begin to doubt yourself,
and fill the voids in your mind with negativity as opposed to positivity,
then you will surely fail.
Take a step back and really be honest with yourself and what you've done in your past.
Look at your life and the things that you've done versus the things that you said you wanted to do.
How much of it were you actually able to accomplish?
How badly did you want things in your past?
What were you willing to sacrifice?
Think back to it.
Think back to the day that you set some of your goals
and just how enthusiastic you were back then.
How do you feel about them now?
What's changed in your life since then?
You see, many people like to make up excuses for why they no longer want something that they wanted so badly in their lives before.
But, this usually isn't their fault;
it's a subconscious process.
When the ego realizes that something is going to cause more pain than pleasure, it reverts to the inner wrangling of the mind to come up with valid excuses.
That's because the human mind is incredibly powerful.
It can concoct and conceive of things that are unavailable to the conscious mind.
It can do so much of this in the subconscious that we're merely unaware of the processes it takes to reach its decisions.
If, one day, you wake up and realize that you no longer want what you wanted in the past because it was too hard to achieve,
or maybe impossible to achieve,
then the ego did its job.
When you wake up one day with a clear excuse why you no longer want that goal anymore, then the ego did a very good job, in fact.
When the ego can convince you that you don't want something anymore in your life, and come up with some very valid excuses why, then it's doing its job perfectly well.
However, this is all so difficult to see on a conscious level.
So much of our pride is wrapped up in our goals,
that when we fall down and can't achieve them,
the very fragile inner self has a difficult time coping.
This is when we're the most vulnerable.
And, depending on how lofty your goals were in the past, if you fell down, then you most likely fell down hard.
Or, if you've never had lofty goals, and you've always played it safe,
then your inner self probably hasn't been too bruised.
However, like most other people,
you've probably experienced some failure in your life.
You've probably been hurt and bruised when you failed at something.
What did you do in the face of that failure?
How did you approach it?
Did you shut yourself off from the world?
Or did you push even harder?
Were you willing to take no for an answer or did you just throw your hands up in silent resignation when you started to panic about all the negativity surrounding a certain situation?
I know that it's not that easy to look back at our personal situations from an honest perspective because of how powerful the ego can be,
but it's important to do so.
It's critical to be able to look at our lives from an open and honest perspective.
+Finding your Source of Happiness
Attaining happiness is something that seems to be fleeting for most people.
Most people chase happiness but never get there.
They think that some amount of money or the attainment of some tangible item is going to do it.
Or, even that a certain relationship, job, or trip to a far-off place will help them achieve happiness.
But, what most people don't realize is that, happiness comes from within.
Any amount of happiness that can be achieved from external things will never last.
We will always want to move on to the next bigger, better thing.
That's simply how the human mind works.
No matter what you have today, one day, long ago, you thought it would bring you happiness.
And, if today that thing doesn't bring you happiness, what do you think changed about it?
What's different about having that thing in your life now?
Whether it was a relationship, a house, a car, a job, or anything else, you once wanted that.
You once wanted it and probably thought that it would bring you happiness, so what's different?
Nothing.
The only difference is internal.
It has nothing to do with the external "thing."
Why is any of this important?
I bring up happiness because so many of us out there are striving to achieve things because we think it will make us happy.
We want a better job because we'll make more money and be happier.
Or, we want a bigger house because we'll be more comfortable and be happier.
We want things for what we feel they will bring us.
But, when we don't really get to the true source of what it is that's driving us,
we can never really be happy.
I say this because happiness truly is a choice.
We have to look to others who are less fortunate rather than those that have more.
It's okay to aspire to achieve certain things in life,
but not at the cost of your happiness.

Thói quen xấu được hình thành trong nhiều năm.
Nếu bạn đã quen với việc bước qua cửa trước, ngồi xuống ghế trường kỷ, bật ti vi lên rồi ngồi xem suốt hàng giờ liền,
thì thói quen này sẽ cản trở bạn thực hiện ước mơ.

Chẳng có cách nào dễ dàng để từ bỏ thói quen xấu cả.
Thật ra, việc này cực kỳ khó khăn.
Để thay đổi thói quen lâu năm của tâm trí cùng cơ thể, ta phải kiên trì hành động trong suốt thời gian dài.
Nhưng thói quen xấu thật ra là gì?
Chúng bắt nguồn từ đâu và được hình thành ra sao?
Bằng cách hiểu được mình tạo ra các thói quen xấu của bản thân, bạn sẽ khám phá ra một số điều bí ẩn giải thích được lý do tại sao bạn làm cái mình làm.
